newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK stocks end sharply off after volatile session.
newsitem.headline: HK stocks end sharply off after volatile session.

text.p: Hong Kong's Hang Seng index posted its biggest point decline since July on Thursday, ending sharply lower after futures-linked volatility drove it to an early record high before prices succumbed to profit-taking.
The Hang Seng index whipsawed in a range of 444 points before closing the day down 220.19 points at 13,310.76. The blue chip index hit an all-time intra-day high at 13,744.30.
"It's all over the place," said Miles Remington, sales trader at Crosby Securities. "Volume is obscene."
Turnover was a heavy HK$13.58 billion compared to HK$13.42 billion on Wednesday.
Thursday's decline was the biggest point decline since July 8 when the index fell 287.08 points.
November Hang Seng index futures expired on Thursday and closed 149 points lower at 13,491. December futures fell 275 points to 13,400.
Analysts said the leap in prices at the opening was linked to the expiration.

"The main thing is the futures index is just leading the cash market," said Ricky Tam, senior research analyst at Delta Asia Securities. "The futures market just jumped so quickly. There was a huge short squeeze today."
The Stock Exchange of Hong Kong said it was looking into the unusual trading activity at Thursday's opening.

"We are examining the opening transactions in a number of stocks and going to the brokers involved in those transactions and asking them to explain what took place," said Paul Phenix, executive director of the exchange's compliance division.

The Hang Seng later shed all of its early gains, with some investors taking profits ahead of Thursday's U.S. Thanksgiving Day holiday. "The U.S. market is not going to give us any lead overnight simply because it is closed. Therefore I would expect a relatively quiet day tomorrow," said Remington.
He said stocks were looking overbought and volatility had been expected.

Among the big movers, HSBC Holdings was ramped up to a record HK$168.50 before ending the session down HK$2.50 at HK$161.00. Sun Hung Kai Properties jumped to an early new high at HK$101.50 but closed on a loss of HK$1.00 at HK$97.00.

The market's tumble took some of the early shine of Jackin International shares, which made their market debut on Thursday. The stock opened at HK$2.325 per share compared with an issue price of HK$1.05 per share and closed at HK$1.99.
